items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: And there was a girl there, no relation, but her name was Zella Hunter, playing piano.

ctx.x: Wait a minute. That place was Dago Frank's. That was Dago Frank's. (PHONETIC). And that was the very first nightclub, or cabaret, that I worked in, see. And so I stayed there until... that was in the sporting district, you know. So I stayed there until they closed Dago Frank's. See. When they closed Dago Frank's, in the meantime different people had been hearing about me, you see. Because I started off down there singing my little -- singing the songs they had, "All Night Long," and "Where the River Shannon…

And so by that time, different ones had kind of heard there was a pretty good singer down at Dago Frank's. So I went up to the place called Hugh Hoskins (PHONETIC), that was at 32nd and State. Hugh Hoskins. And there was a girl there, no relation, but her name was Zella Hunter, playing piano. And I went to Hugh Hoskins and I started singing the blues. And I sang my little blues that I had picked out on the piano in my hometown in Memphis, you know. I had picked it out with my finger because I don't know one note…
